To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phase of alpha oscillations at the time of a visual target onset determines whether the target will be perceived or ignored.
Alpha phase and power modulate visual awareness for spatially uncued stimuli.
alpha phase is a marker of spatial attentional bias, and alpha power is a marker of temporal attentional bias.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oscillatory brain rhythms in attentional processing.
the mechanisms underlying visual attention.
the question of how the brain processes and integrates information from the outside world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alpha oscillations are not only involved in spatial attention, but that alpha phase also modulates temporal attention.
alpha oscillations are involved in the inhibition of visual processing in unattended space, but that this inhibition can also be modulated in a temporal manner.
the power and phase of alpha oscillations reveal an interaction between spatial and temporal visual attention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alpha oscillations are a pulsating mechanism that inhibits visual processing in both spatial and temporal domains.
alpha phase and amplitude changes can bias information processing to attended space and time.
attention is a dynamic process, and alpha oscillations are a key component of this process, which modulates visual processing in space and time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the alpha phase of the entrained rhythm can bias attention to a specific time window.
alpha oscillations are not only a lateralized inhibition but also a temporal inhibition, and that the two are related.
oscillatory activity in the alpha band is not only modulated by spatial attention, but also by temporal attention and that both spatial and temporal attention are interdependent in the brain.
